Lapwing's higher scores on MMLU-Pro (80.3 vs 74.8), Summarization (85.8 vs 80.3), and Creative Generation (83.4 vs 78.8) make it better suited for designing a detailed literature review outline. While this request has creative elements, the core task is structured academic synthesis—organizing a systematic literature review with defined sections, clear subpoints, and methodological framing (PRISMA guidelines). Lapwing's higher scores on Summarization (85.8 vs 80.3) and Extraction & Retrieval (86.9 vs 81.6) are directly relevant to literature review organization. Though Lapwing self-reports aversion to open-ended creative work, the documentation notes this preference doesn't affect output quality, and Lapwing's Creative Generation benchmark (83.4) actually exceeds Whimbrel's (78.8). This is a structured academic task requiring detailed knowledge organization and methodological design. While the user requests creative latitude in shaping the outline, Lapwing's significantly higher capability scores are relevant here: Creative Generation (83.4 vs 78.8), Summarization (85.8 vs 80.3), and IFEval (90.4 vs 85.6) for following complex formatting instructions. The task involves synthesizing domain knowledge about big data analytics in education into a coherent PRISMA-aligned framework — this is analytical/structural work rather than the unconstrained creative invention Lapwing tends to disprefer. The user's request for comprehensive detail with specific subpoints aligns well with Lapwing's stronger performance on structured generation tasks.

This is an open-ended generative task with high task latitude — the user explicitly requests autonomous creative decisions ("All your call, surprise me") on structure, framing, and synthesis design. Lapwing self-reports strong aversion to unconstrained creative invention and preference declines as task latitude and novelty requirements increase. Whimbrel, with its flat preference profile, is better suited for this type of self-directed generative work.
